newsitem.title: GERMANY: Greenpeace keeps up fight against gene-soymeal.
newsitem.headline: Greenpeace keeps up fight against gene-soymeal.

text.p: Environmental group Greenpeace at a press conference on Tuesday called for the labelling of feeds containing gene-altered soybeans from the United States.
Country merchants should clearly indicate the content of meals and feeds prior to sales to farmers, said the biotechnology expert at the German Greenpeace branch, Joerg Naumann in a statement.
A Greenpeace poll taken among 1,004 farmers showed that 70 percent did not wish to use feedstuffs made from genetically modified raw materials, he said.
Some 90 percent demanded labelling of such feeds.

Naumann warned food scares about beef infected with the "madcow," brain-waisting disease, had demonstrated the choice of feed ingredients could be directly related to future consumer acceptance of meat.

Greenpeace says that genetically altered U.S. soybeans, which are imported and crushed in Europe, may bring unknown health risks and should therefore be traded and labelled separately to allow sceptical consumers a choice.
The beans have been developed by U.S. chemicals firm Monsanto to resist its weedkiller Roundup.
Some 80 percent of imported beans in Europe, which this season may contain up to two percent of gene-altered material, are processed into meal for animal feeding.
European Union Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler last week tabled proposals for the compulsory labelling of gene-modified animal feeds, following a more moderate plan by the Environment Commissioner.
